newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian ministers to head for Iraqi trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian ministers to head for Iraqi trade talks.

text.p: Jordan's ministers of trade and energy will travel to Baghdad on Wednesday to try to resolve differences with Iraq holding up agreement on a 1997 trade protocol, an official said on Tuesday.

Trade and Industry Minister Ali Abu al-Ragheb and Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Hashem Dabbas will hold talks in Iraq "to continue negotiations on the supply of oil to Jordan and the trade protocol," the official said.

Sanctions-hit Iraq has supplied Jordan with around 75,000 barrels per day of cheap oil in return for Jordanian goods under an annual trade protocol which is exempt from the strict U.N. embargo slapped on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Jordan said it halved the value of goods sent to Iraq last year to $220 million because it said Iraq was accruing heavy debts under the previous accords. This year Jordan is also seeking a seven percent increase in Iraqi oil supplies, Dabbas said earlier this month.
Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz said on Monday his country was committed to supplying Jordan with oil, but queried Jordan's debt claim.
Jordanian businessmen, who are paid by Jordan's Central Bank for goods sent to Iraq under the protocol, have called for an increase in its volume this year.
